params.body:
The terms and the privacy policy are what a buyer and Mollie read to learn what they agree to. Several clauses described a product the site does not sell, or a flow it does not have. This brings them in line with the billing code. Both documents stay marked as drafts for legal review: this fixes the facts, not the legal wording.

## Terms (version 1.1)

- **Organisations only** (articles 1, 2, 6, 16, 18). Article 2 says paid plans are sold to organisations, with the details asked before payment. Article 6 described a consumer withdrawal flow with consent at checkout, which the checkout never had. It now says the consumer withdrawal right does not apply. The consumer carve-outs in liability and jurisdiction are gone. The article numbers stay, so the cross-references hold.
- **Plans** (article 4):
  - Decode loses the yearly price of EUR 2,990, which the site does not sell.
  - Decode and Intelligence read "annual plan billed monthly", as on the pricing page.
  - Intelligence was "invoiced quarterly"; it is billed monthly.
- **VAT** (article 4): Belgian VAT in Belgium; reverse charge elsewhere in the EU with a VAT number confirmed in VIES, and no paid plan without one; no Belgian VAT outside the EU. This is `App\Billing\Vat`.
- **Payment and cancellation** (article 5):
  - Mollie charges in EUR, and Trendwolves NV invoices every payment.
  - Cancelling works from the account page, not only by mail.
  - Moving up and down works as `Subscriptions::change` does it.
  - An unpaid renewal ends the plan after fourteen days (`BILLING_GRACE_DAYS`).

## Privacy policy (version 1.1)

- It said the site keeps only Mollie's customer and subscription references. Since #249 it also keeps the billing details and the VIES result, plus a record of every payment, refund and chargeback, which goes to the Trendwolves bookkeeping. The policy now says so.

## Left as it was, for Trendwolves to decide

- Decode and Intelligence "renew for successive twelve month terms unless cancelled at least thirty days before". After the first year the site carries on month by month and does not hold the thirty days.
- The named-user limits: up to four on Decode, up to ten on Intelligence. The site does not count them.
- Accounting records are kept "seven years".

## Tests

- New `TermsPageTest` case for the clauses above, plus the privacy wording. The version check moves to 1.1. The existing check that the contract prices match the pricing page still passes.
- Full suite: 594 of 595 pass. The one failure is `BuildStampTest`, which fails in every worktree because it reads the checkout's own build stamp. Pint clean.
params.title: Terms and privacy policy say what the site sells and does
